Messages.Author: tetragr...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
I'm here with a question about the single action per turn.
I think that is allright, but i need some clarifications about it.
I was reading that a minion can take an
"Enter in Combat with another minion" action
(via Haven Uncovered, for example) and eventually
repeat the same action (if he can untap in the same turn)
as long as it is provided by a different card or another copy
of Haven Uncovered in play. If this is true, i feel
a little inconsistency in the general "single action x turn"
rule logic.
"Entering in combat with another minion"
should be considered a type action of its own, even if it's not
listed in the original Vtes rule booklet.
A consistent number of vampires and minions can take it
as a special ability, and lots of cards allow our minions/vampires to
attempt it.
For example, i don't see the reason why Wynn can take the action to
enter in combat with a Vampire by its own unique ability, untap
via Freak or sup EarthMeld, and then enter in combat again with a Bum's
rush or similar card. The action(s) type is (almost)the same.
While Donatien cannot attempt to bleed in the same turn (if he is
untapped) after he bled a Methuselah via its own unique ability.
I think that if a minion can't attempt to equip, recruit
allies/retainers etc., more than one time in the same turn, then i
think that he should not be able to repeat
"Enter in combat with another..." actions too.
Otherwise i feel here a little unbalancing in favor of rush-untapping
decks
Maybe this question was already debated, still i'm unsure if the stuff
above is right, so clarifications are very welcome.
Thanks in advice.
TetratheM

P.S.: can someone tell me why the ammo cards cannot be used with the
ZipGun? Is the combo with Dragonsbreaths too cheap to play with?
Thanks again.

Messages.Author: Sorrow
Messages.Body:
> It is my understanding that you can not do as you mentioned. If a
> vampire bleeds with social charms he can not come back and bleed with
> media influence. Therefore why would you be able to enter combat thru
> a haven uncovered and then use a bum's rush? In my play group this is
> not allowed. And, I believe the ruling on single action would also
> prohibit this.

But it is allowed for the very reason the original poster mentioned
early in his post: "Entering Combat" is not an action type like, say,
bleeding is. "Social Charm" and "Media Influence" are the same
action type and as such are illegal to play by the same minion on
the same turn. However, "Bum's Rush" and "Haven Uncovered"
(and vamp's special abilities) are not of a particular action type. As
such, are each either own actions as defined by their card name
and instance. So you could not Bum's Rush, untap, Bum's Rush
again because it would violate NRA. But you could Bum's Rush,
untap, Ambush. Also bear in mind that card instance is very
important in cards with undefined action types. This makes it
so that each instance of Haven Uncovered is a different action
because each is a seperate instance. So this is legal: attack
vamp A via Haven on it, untap, attack vamp C via Haven on
it, untap, attack vamp H via Haven on it, etc.

This leads me to a question for LSJ: IIRC, you said in a previous
thread that each vote to burn an Anarch Revolt is a seperate type
of vote as defined by each instance, I guess much in the same way
that each Haven is it's own instance so that you can perform the
example I gave above. But since burning an AR is a political
action (whereas Haven is not a defined action), I don't see how it
can be that if a Delaying Tactics is played during a vote to burn
an AR, another minion during that same turn can call a vote to
burn a totally different AR. Yes, it's a different instance in play,
but it is still the same political action and card name. By that
logic, one could take it a bit further and say "Well, yes, you
Delaying Tactics that minion's attempt to call a ConAg, but now
this minion is trying to call it and since it is not being called using
the same card (instance) as the minion before, this is a different
instance and as such, this new minion can attempt to call it no
matter what Delaying Tactics says".
Since AR is part of a larger defined type of actions, I don't see
how it can have the same 'instance exemption' that Haven can
have with regards to multiple actions, especially with regards to
Delaying Tactics.

Sorrow

In article <371252AA...@alpinetaxi.com>,
Patrick Harris <alp...@alpinetaxi.com> wrote:
> > There is no action type defined called "Move blood to an
uncontrolled
> > vampire." Because there is not, you may take multiple different
actions to
> > do so as long as you have the appropriate skills/titles.
>
> Is there a list somewhere of the "defined action types"? Or can you
list
> them out if there aren't many? It would be handy to know which are
allowed
> and which aren't.

From the Standard DCI Floor Rules:

2.5.1 No Repeat Actions
A given minion may not repeat an action, by action type, in a single
turn.

The defined "action types" are: bleed, hunt, equip, employ retainer,
recruit ally, political action, leave torpor, rescue a
vampire from torpor, and diablerize a vampire in torpor.

If an action card is used to perform one of these actions, that action
is considered to be of that type. If it is not one of
these actions (i.e., Bum's Rush), then it is a type of its own, by card
name.

If a card in play is used to perform one of these actions, that action
is considered to be of that type. If it is not one of these
actions (i.e., enter combat via Haven Uncovered), then it is a type of
its own, by specific instance of the card in play.

Example: A vampire that successfully bleeds its controller's prey via
Computer Hacking, then untaps via Freak Drive, cannot
perform any bleeding action again, of any kind whatsoever, in that same
turn.

Carpe Noctem.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 14 Feb 2000 ravnos...@my-deja.com wrote:
> It is my understanding that you can not do as you mentioned. If a
> vampire bleeds with social charms he can not come back and bleed with
> media influence. Therefore why would you be able to enter combat thru
> a haven uncovered and then use a bum's rush? In my play group this is
> not allowed. And, I believe the ruling on single action would also
> prohibit this.

No, it doesn't.

The NRA rule prohibits taking any basic defined action e.g. bleed, as per
the rule book. It also prohibits taking the same named card action twice,
even if it provides two separate abilities (e.g. You cannot play Scouting
Mission at inferior and superior). However, if there are several copies
of a card in play (e.g. multiple copies of Aggressive Tactics) a separate
action may be taken by the text of each one.

The basic actions defined in the rule book are:

Bleed, Hunt, Recruit Ally, Employ Retainer, Call a Political Action,
Encounter in Torpor (Rescue), Encounter in Torpor (Diablerie) and that's
it, I think.

Enter combat with a minion is *not* a defined action type, therefore you
can happily, if you wanted, enter combat with a minion via:

Bum's Rush
Ambush
Wynn's special rush action (or Beast, Ebanezer, Roxanne)
Bloodhunt (the action card)
Imperial Decree
Covenant of Blood
Huang, Blood Cultist being attackable
Rushing an Unacceptable !Nos
Cardinal Sin: Insubordination
Archon's rush ability
Judgement: Death to the Brujah!
Haven Uncovered
Political Struggle
Purity of the Beast
Monomancy

all on the same turn, assuming untaps. I wonder how many of those it
would be possible to get, in one go, assuming everything had been set up
perfectly. (Not counting, say, multiple different Havens).

Combat is, generally, such a difficult strategy to pull off that the
situation being as it is is not generally a problem, as far as I can see.

Also, if you start defining new action types, you have problems. Can I
play superior Scounting Mission and superior Govern the Unaligned, which
are similar actions? Would you want to define a new action type for that?

--

James Coupe

Essentially, that was the reasoning behind it. Being able to pull a Zip
Gun and fire and torporise a vampire was the standard tactic of a weenie
deck. It was going to torpor anyway, most likely, so it didn't give a
monkey's about the 1 damage it did to itself, and the cost of that weighed
against torporising another vampire is generally small. Too small, in
some opinions.

Whether one agrees with that, or not, of course, is a different matter.
That was, however, the reasoning, as far as I can tell. (This was not an
instance where, in the official document, LSJ provide a hashed-out (i.e.
not part of the official ruling) commentary.)

I believe this was for the purposes of Delaying Tactics only, not NRA, and
the confusion arises because Delaying Tactics affects not just the calling
vampire (who is affected by NRA) but also others (who are not).

Delaying Tactics prevents any other vampire you control from calling the
"same" political action.

If I have two Anarchs in play, and you have two vampires, you use the
first vampire (say, Carlotta Giovanni) to call a vote to burn the the
first Anarch Revolt. I play Delaying Tactics.

"Any vampire. Only usable during a political action. The political action
is cancelled. Untap the acting vampire. The controller of the acting
minion takes the political card if any back into his or her hand, and his
or her minions cannot take the same political action this turn."

The "same political action", for the purposes of Delaying Tactics, refers
only to that specific Anarch Revolt. Rudolpho Giovanni, say, could call a
vote to burn the second Anarch Revolt. But if you had a third vampire,
they could not call a vote to burn Anarch Revolt, as per Delaying Tactics.

--

James Coupe

While the argument could be made, the ruling has already been made:

Terminology
* "Same Action" means: 1) The same inherent (cardless) action taken
against the same target. 2) The action taken with the same card played
from hand, regardless of target. 3) The same action provided by the
same copy of a card in play. (Each action provided by a card in play is
a distinct action (and doesn't count as the "same action").
[RTR 05-SEP-1995]

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 14 Feb 2000 ceci...@my-deja.com wrote:
> I believe that the use of a directed action (D) to enter combat with
> another minion is considered to be an action.

It is an action. It is not, however, a defined *type* of action in the
rule book. Hence, because of the wording of NRA, rushing with an ambush,
rushing with a Haven and rushing with an Archon are all distinct action
types, regardless of the similarness of their effects.

As LSJ has already stated, if you go down this road, you start introducing
more problems - is burning a location an action type? Is moving blood to
a younger uncontrolled vampire an action type? There are, of course,
other instances of this.

--

James Coupe

> The part I was unclear about was your rule 1 for being a repeat action. It was the
> same inherent action against the SAME target, impling that you could do the same
> inherent action against diffrent targets.

"Repeat Action" is associated with the DCI "No Repeat Action" rule, which
cares only about same "action type", not just "same action". See [DCI 719]
for rules on "same action type".

The "same action" definition above has no interaction with the "No Repeat
Action" rule - it is only applicable to cards and effects that care about
the "same action": Obedience, Change of Target (both of which specify
weaker versions of the No Repeat Action rule), Delaying Tactics, etc.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Tue, 15 Feb 2000 tetragr...@my-deja.com wrote:
> (D) Enter in combat with XXX
> (D) Burn a Location
> (D) Take control of XXX

I would ask why you think any of these necessary? Are you finding rush
combat overly powerful? If you are, you are possibly not placing the
right combat defence in your decks. Rush combat is actually quite easy to
throw up defences against - Protean (Flesh of Marble) and Fortitude
(repeatedly prevent) working well against guns, Potence IG, Claws, lids
etc., and only having real problems with a few of the unpreventable
damage/not damage strikes.

Similarly, I cannot see that Arson, Rampage, Al-Ashrad (or any others)
provide such a powerful swing in the game as to require them to be clipped
down in such a manner, nor (D) Take Control. Most of the take control
cards aren't going to get you vampires very easily for very long, without
a lot of work (e.g. rush combat, claw, Graverobbbing) - which I don't see
as needing neutering by NRA, it already has a hard time pulling itself off
anyway.

--

James Coupe

Complicated or not, I think he raises a valid point.
But before I go much further, I'd like to say that my position on this
undecided.

Why should it be that, with regards to NRA, only a small number of actions
are limited (because they just happen to be "defined") whereas others are
not
so limited. "Entering Combat" = "Entering Combat" regardless of the action
took
to initate it. Using Bums Rush, Ambush, Haven, etc. is still 'Entering
Combat'
no matter how you look at it. You say tomatoe I say tomatoe. Similarly,
"Burning a Location" = "Burning a Location", regardless of the action took.
Ambush, Bums Rush, Beast, Wynn, Arson, Bomb, etc, etc. all use the same
term: "Enter combat with.." or "Burn a Location", etc, etc. The only
difference
is that in some cases there are qualifications (ie, with a tapped minion,
etc).
These qualifications do not change the fact that it is still an "Entering
Combat"
action. So since it must be that things like bleeding, equipping, hunting,
policitcal actions, etc. should be limited, why not too those actions that
are
pretty similar not only in type but in wording. "Enter Combat" is no more
difficult to remember as an action type than, say, bleed is.

While I agree that action types such as those that allow you to take control
of
X are not as universally similar with regards to wording and as such cannot
be as easily classified, but the likes as "Enter Combat" and "Burn a
Location"
(and I think there may be one or two more that are slipping my mind at the
moment) could easily be "defined" and as such fall under the constraints of
NRA.

Sorrow

Well, it's slightly complicated, but it's fairly easy to recognize
when something is a "basic" action type. Bleeding, for example. It's
also fairly easy for new players to recognize why bleed, majesty,
bleed, majesty, bleed, majesty, bleed is such a bad thing, so they are
a lot more disposed towards learning the complications.

>A one where players don't have to remember "defined" "undefined" action
>types and so on. Maybe it will prove futile, as the NRA as it is now is
>the simpler rule possible, still i would like to get
>some discussion about this:
>there's a chanche to get a simpler NRA rule?
>A very simple one can be: "A minion can take only one action per turn".

Reduces Freak Drive, Rutor's Hand, Precognizant Mobility, and
Alexandra to wallpaper, as there is no longer a point to untapping
with these cards (replace each with a Wake, since the surprise value
is almost always worth more than the deterrent value). Removes
several other Fortitude cards from play, as nobody is going to try to
Rapid Healing themselves out of torpor on the NEXT turn - someone will
diablerize. Makes big vampires even more useless (Freak Drive and
Rutor's Hand are excellent methods of getting multiple actions out of
one vamp, which is necessary for big vamps to compete against a
smaller-cap deck).

>Untapping effect would be reduced to a defense purpose only.
>(i untap and get a minion untapped ready for defense).

except, again, it's better to have a Wake in hand, since your predator
will then exercise your defenses, cycling your deck to its offensive
cards. Even if you're only going to hurl a body in front of the
steamroller, Wake is better since you get to select which body,
instead of "which vampire can untap."

-- Derek
